reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents Forsage's extraordinary income and community claims for criticism and exposure rather than encouraging viewers to join or invest. The speaker calls the subject a scam, questions claims such as millions of users and very high income, and asks viewers to share the video for a more detailed discussion.

First he writes that in Forsage so far more than 1200000 people have taken income of up to 150000 from 10 million. And then what?
Friends, if you want more detailed video on ForceZ, then share this video as much as you can.

opening.argument: The video links an unusually large earnings promise to concrete participation steps. Its Forsage graphic says registration is open, displays “1 Crore Earning,” and instructs viewers to log in to an account, creating a direct reward-and-action pathway rather than merely discussing cryptocurrency. Another displayed account-style graphic pairs an income figure of 14 lakh 70 thousand with a WhatsApp contact prompt and visible profit figures. Taken together, the presentation gives viewers a simple route from contact or login to an extraordinary financial opportunity, which is characteristic of a scam solicitation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the subject a scam does not erase the video's repeated use of promotional material. The narration itself repeats the extraordinary claims about Forsage income and user numbers, while the visuals show registration, login, earnings, and contact prompts. Asking viewers to share the video can also increase the reach of those promotional claims, regardless of the speaker's stated criticism.

citations.quote: First he writes that in Forsage so far more than 1200000 people have taken income of up to 150000 from 10 million. And then what?

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited graphics show claims being displayed, but they do not establish that viewers are being asked to register, log in, contact anyone, or provide money by this video's speaker. The narration explicitly frames the subject as something whose scam will be exposed and questions the income claims, so the visuals function as evidence under criticism rather than a solicitation.

opening.argument: Several red flags appear together: a very large income figure, an affiliate-program structure, a WhatsApp contact route, and payment into a wallet. The Forsage post describes an affiliate program and claims that more than one lakh to fifty lakh can be earned, while the same material refers to money being paid into a Trust wallet. The combination of tiered participation language, dramatic returns, external messaging, and crypto-wallet payment presents a high-risk recruitment scheme, even if the narrator couches the presentation as commentary.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The fact that the narrator mocks the claims does not make the underlying marketing signals disappear. The video gives substantial screen time to income figures, affiliate language, wallet payment, and WhatsApp contact details. A careful viewer could reasonably understand that the opportunity being shown is built around recruitment and unusually high earnings, not ordinary financial education.

citations.quote: And in the next point he writes that In the same time, Forsage has become the biggest billionaire in lockdown.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Those red flags belong to material the video is examining, not to an offer made by the speaker. The narration calls the claims fraudulent, questions their wording, and says the video will expose the scam. The frames do not show the speaker instructing viewers to join, pay, recruit, or use a wallet.

opening.argument: Although the speaker adopts a critical tone, the video's practical effect can still be promotional. It repeatedly displays Forsage branding, income screenshots, an affiliate-program description, and a direct contact prompt, while also highlighting claims of millions of participants and extraordinary earnings. Showing these concrete aspirational examples gives the opportunity visibility and social proof. The closing request to share the video further distributes the branded material, allowing the presentation to steer viewers toward the opportunity even while framing itself as an investigation.

citations.quote: Friends, if you want more detailed video on ForceZ, then share this video as much as you can.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference account assumes that critical wording controls the video's overall effect, but the branded graphics and income examples remain prominent and memorable. The viewer is shown the opportunity's apparent scale, earnings, affiliate structure, and contact route. The request to share expands circulation of that material, so the warning format does not conclusively prevent promotional impact.

citations.quote: First he writes that in Forsage so far more than 1200000 people have taken income of up to 150000 from 10 million. And then what?

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The promotional interpretation overlooks the speaker's consistent criticism: he says the scam will be exposed, challenges the advertised income and user figures, and mocks the wording of the claims. Sharing is explicitly requested for a more detailed video, not for registration or participation. The branded examples are therefore presented as objects of investigation, not endorsements.
